miles (customer): hey - running into a weird one with /v1/rerank/batch. scores seem shifted across queries and sometimes the scores array is shorter than candidates. started after we upgraded our client lib. payload + response below. this is blocking our release :/

zoe (support): sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact curl you used (redact keys) and the raw response body? also how big are your batches (#queries x candidates each)?

miles (customer): sure. samples: 3 queries, expected per-query candidate counts = [2,0,3] (query 2 has intentionally zero candidates). payload: 
```json
{
  "queries": ["q1","q2","q3"],
  "candidates": [
    ["c1","c2"],
    [],
    ["c3","c4","c5"]
  ]
}
```
curl we used: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @payload.json
```
response we got (trimmed):
```json
{
  "scores": [
    [0.84, 0.76],
    [0.65, 0.12, 0.05]
  ],
  "error": null
}
```
notice scores length is 2 arrays only, and the 2nd array has 3 scores which look like they belong to queries 2+3 merged. also some scores are negative in other runs.

zoe (support): thanks — that helps. two immediate hypotheses: 1) client serialized empty arrays differently and our unpacking logic in the batch path collapses empty lists, 2) there was an encode/flatten transformation bug where we turn nested candidates into flat + counts and counts got miscomputed (off-by-one when an empty list is present). can you confirm your client is sending an explicit empty array for q2 and not `null` or omitting the key?

miles (customer): confirmed - we send `[]`. we started using a new helper that does `candidates.filter(Boolean)` before sending (to remove falsy entries). it looks like it might be removing the empty array entirely.

sam (eng-ml): tagging in — this matches a repro I just ran locally. our batch rerank endpoint internally flattens candidates and uses `per_query_counts` to slice the flat array. if a client omits an empty candidate list, the counts vector is shorter, and the runtime mistakenly reuses the next counts value — resulting in merged score arrays. we've got a failing unit test that covers this.

sam (eng-ml): repro steps I used: 
1) payload with explicit empty arrays vs payload with empty arrays omitted.
2) run `pytest tests/integration/test_batch_rerank.py::test_empty_query_handling`
3) observed mismatch.

sam (eng-ml): workaround for customers: ensure the client preserves empty lists (do not filter them out). or construct and send `per_query_candidate_counts` explicitly as a top-level param (we accept both formats).

maria (sre): also worth checking rate/latency — when clients do large batches we hit longer scheduler queuing which can interleave messages in logs and make debugging harder. any 401/429s in your logs? those could indicate clients retrying and mixing payloads.

miles (customer): we did see a couple 401s yesterday when our token rotated but not during this particular run. latency was ~1.2s which is ok. the issue reproduces reliably if I remove the empty array in the payload.

zoe (support): ok. we'll treat this as two parts: 1) short-term mitigation + customer guidance, 2) a code fix to make the server resilient to missing empty arrays. i've opened SUP-1120 to track the customer escalation and PR linking.

sam (eng-ml): patch is ready — we now coerce missing candidate lists into empty counts during unpack. PR: https://git.internal.redwood/eng/serving/pulls/4021 (tests added). i'm going to request a hotfix deploy.

eng-deploy-bot: rolling_deploy started for `serving-batch-rerank` (sha: a1b2c3d) — will run canary in prod/us-west-2; expected 10m.

miles (customer): thank you — i'll validate after the canary. can you also confirm if this could have affected billing (we appear to have token counts billed for merged candidates)?

zoe (support): good question — billing counts tokens based on the actual request payload we received (flat tokens). if your client omitted an empty array, the server billed tokens for the flattened candidates present. merged scores don't change token billing, but misalignment can cause you to attribute spend to wrong queries in your analytics. i'll loop in billing if you want us to audit the invoice.

maria (sre): deployed hotfix passed canary, pushed to prod in us-west-2. watch logs for `batch_rerank:coerce_missing_empty_lists` flag.

sam (eng-ml): summary of root cause: client-side filter dropped empty arrays -> server unpack assumed counts matched queries -> off-by-one slicing -> scores associated with wrong queries. fix adds defensive coercion plus an integration test to catch this.

miles (customer): verified on our side after the deploy — responses now have 3 arrays in `scores`: for q1,q2,q3 (q2 empty array). all good here. thanks for quick turnaround :thumbsup:

zoe (support): awesome — closing SUP-1120 after we confirm billing audit if you want one. reopen if anything else shows up.

eng-deploy-bot: deploy completed: serving-batch-rerank @ prod/us-west-2 (a1b2c3d) — 200/200 healthy.
